data.narrative:
Lab 91, a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Anand Chamarthy that has raised $10M+, sits within a competitive peer universe of 11 comparable companies across public and private markets. The private comparable set includes 8 firms at similar or adjacent stages, anchored by peers like Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched. Public Semiconductors benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) trade at a median 18.4x price-to-sales but cannot be directly applied due to Lab 91's undisclosed revenue.

Two valuation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $10M raised as a proxy base and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $25M. Peer-median analysis of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—SambaNova Systems ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B)—produces a median valuation of $2.3B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $11.0B. The wide dispersion reflects meaningful performance variance within the peer cohort.

Triangulating these two methods yields a range of $21M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median estimate of $1.2B. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects the tension between Lab 91's early funding stage and comparable valuations of more advanced peers. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation, capital efficiency relative to peers, and time-to-revenue—factors that would justify positioning within this range.
